texts: People travel hundreds of miles to dip in the holy waters at the Kumbh and come out believing every sin is gone, yet the mind that went in dirty walks out exactly as dirty as before.
holy dip, dirty mind
doha on people who take a dip in Ganga and think all their sins vanish
The body is washed in sacred waters; the soul sits on the bank, still unwashed.
My uncle goes to Haridwar every year to wash away his sins, and every year he cheats his tenants again by March. Could you write a doha about him?
Sandalwood cools the bathed skin, but the heat of the heart is not put out by any holy dip.
holy dip, sandalwood
My mother-in-law bathes at dawn in the holy waters, rubs sandalwood on her arms, and tells me I am impure for sleeping late. What would Kabir say to her?
Write about the pilgrim who bathes in the holy waters at dawn and smears sandalwood paste on his skin, believing he is made clean and fragrant, though the stink of envy still clings to his mind.
doha about bathing in holy places and putting on sandalwood but staying dirty inside
The crow dips in the sacred waters and comes out still black; so the sinner, bathed, remains a sinner.
doha: a crow bathing in holy water doesn't turn white
A doha about the crow which dips again and again in the sacred waters and yet remains as black as before, like the pilgrim whose body is bathed daily but whose heart is darkened by greed and deceit.
Our family goes to bathe at the holy ghat every year, and last year a crow stole my sandwich as I came out. Dad said even the crow had no sins, and the rest of us had many. Doha?
crow, holy bath
In the holy waters the pilgrims splash like children, but the stain of the mind is not so easily rinsed.

Write a doha on the crowd that jostles on the ghat to dip in the sacred waters at the auspicious hour, pushing the weak aside, and goes home certain that every sin has been washed away by that single dip.
ghat, pilgrim bath
write something about bathing in a sacred place to wash off sins lol
At the Kumbh my cousin pushed an old lady aside to get to the water first, and then said a prayer of thanks for being cleansed. I'd love a doha about that
bath daily, mind unclean
doha: you can wash your body all day, the mind needs washing too
A doha for the one who bathes three times a day and prays for the washing away of sins, but never once washes the thoughts of lust, anger and pride that keep dirtying his mind through the day.
My neighbour showers three times a day and wears pure white, and then gossips for hours about the whole street. Kabir doha for him?
Scrub the skin until it gleams, yet the filth of thought remains in its hidden room.
My grandmother made us wake before sunrise to bathe in the cold holy waters on the festival day, and we came out shivering and she said all our sins were gone. I wonder what Kabir would say. A doha?
A body shivers in the sacred waters; the mind, a comfortable sinner, stays warm and dry.
doha on holy dip tradition and sins not really washing off

Compose a verse on the festival crowds that bathe in the holy waters at the appointed hour and return in joy, certain that their sins are washed, while the cause of sin, the restless mind, was never touched.
festival dip, sins
The temple bathing tank is full of pilgrims scrubbing; no one has asked what the soul has done.
At the temple in our city there is a bathing tank where hundreds wash before they enter, and then they walk in and push each other for a better view. A doha?
doha: washing before entering the temple but your mind is still dirty
temple bath, dirty mind
A doha about the pilgrims who wash in the temple tank before entering the sanctum and think purity is assured, though they carry hatred, jealousy and greed with them through the gates of the temple.
Every morning my father-in-law spends an hour in the bath chanting, and then yells at the maid for a spot on the floor. A doha for his bathing?
bath, sins, unwashed
He bathes for an hour, and still the mind goes unbathed.
Write a Kabir style doha for those who consider that bathing washes away sin, though if water could wash the soul of its sins, the creatures that live in it would long ago have attained liberation.
doha on how bathing in holy places doesnt clean sins
doha about the house of a man who bathes daily but his house is full of fights, and the skeleton in the cupboard
A bath each morning in the house, a skeleton of old sins in the cupboard; no water has reached it.
In our house my uncle has a long morning bath routine, but the family skeleton, an old unpaid debt to his brother, hangs over every dinner. Could you write a doha?
house, skeleton, bath
A doha on the man who keeps his house and body spotlessly clean, scrubs himself daily with holy water, yet hides the skeleton of old crimes in a room that no water or prayer has ever washed.
Sandalwood on the washed limbs, envy on the washed mind; which of the two is perfumed?
After the holy bath, my aunt dabs sandalwood on her wrists and pronounces herself pure, and then speaks cruelly of her sister-in-law. Doha for her?
bath, sandalwood, dirty heart
Compose a doha about those who bathe in the holy waters, rub fragrant sandalwood on their bodies, and believe they have become pure, though the foul smell of ill will rises from their minds.
doha: sandalwood after a holy bath, still stinking inside
My boss bathes in a sacred pool every month and then sacks someone the next day, claiming a clean slate. What would Kabir say? A doha
doha: bathing monthly in holy pools and sinning in between
He washes on the first of the month, and sins on the second, and the water carries only his body.
Write a doha on the one who bathes in the sacred waters, prays for forgiveness, and returns that same week to the same deceit and cruelty, treating the bath as a monthly cleaning of the conscience.
bathing as sin excuse

Write a doha about the fish that lives in the water all its life and the churn that stirs the curd to butter, neither claiming holiness, while the pilgrim bathes in the holy waters expecting purity without effort.

My grandmother, who churns butter every day, says the fish in the pond are more religious than the people who go to bathe in the holy water, since the fish never leave. Could you write a doha about that?
doha: the fish lives in the water its whole life, no salvation, and the churn at least gives butter
The fish lives in the water always, yet no liberation; the churn turns and gives butter at least.
fish, churn, bathing
A man at the ghat dressed in clean clothes dipped three times, and his own shadow showed him a thin frown; he walked out and slapped his son for splashing. The shadow was darker than before. Doha?
shadow, sword, holy dip
The sword of pride is not rinsed away in sacred waters, and the shadow follows the bathed.
doha: holy bath cant wash the sword and the shadow of the mind
A verse about the one who bathes in the sacred waters before sunrise, believing it washes the shadow of his sins, but who then picks up the sword of anger by noon and strikes at all who disagree.
Waves of the holy waters touch the skin and withdraw, never reaching the mind that sits in its dark room.
bath, body only
doha: water only washes the outside
My friend dunked herself in the holy waters during a big festival and posted selfies, and then insulted the girl who took her photo. What a doha that would make
Compose a verse about the sacred bath that touches only the skin and not the mind, because water has never reached the thoughts, and dirt of thought needs repentance and honesty, not a ritual bath.
My father had a weekly trip to the holy waters for what he called 'cleansing', but he never changed any of his habits, even the bad ones. A doha about that?
He goes to the waters to wash his sins, and returns to find them waiting at home.
bathing, sins return
doha: sins waiting on the bank when you come out
Compose a doha on the pilgrim who dips in the holy waters to leave his sins behind, only to find them waiting for him on the bank, ready to follow him home and settle in his heart once more.
The bell at the ghat rang as the pilgrims dipped, and an old woman next to me murmured that the bell rings for the cleansed. I wondered who is truly cleansed. Doha for this?
The bell rings as pilgrims dip, and the heart rings hollow.
A doha about the pilgrims who dip in the holy waters as the bell rings, shout their prayers, and rush out believing they are cleansed, though the one bell that rings in a clean heart has not sounded.
bell, holy dip
doha: a bell rings when you take a holy dip but nothing changes inside
Last month our relatives took us all to wash our sins at the holy ghat, and they spent the whole trip arguing about who would pay. A doha idea?
At the holy ghat the pilgrims bathe; a quarrel waits, unwashed, at their elbows.
doha: family goes on a holy dip trip and fights the whole time
Write a doha about a family that makes a long and costly trip to bathe in the holy waters together, and spends the whole journey in bitter quarrels, returning no cleaner than before.
holy trip, family quarrels
My rich neighbour built a palace with a private bathing pool and says it is for his daily purification, but he is bitter and mean to anyone who visits. Could you write a doha about him?
In his palace he bathes in a pool of marble, but his mind still lives in a muddy ditch.
Write a doha on the king in his palace who bathes in scented water daily, with attendants to wash his feet, and believes that he is purified, though the stain of cruelty on his rule is not removed.
doha: palace has a bathing pool, still a dirty heart
palace, bath, stained heart
Write me a doha about the people who rush to the holy waters on the dark night of the new month, wash away their sins in one plunge, and return to their villages with all their old habits unharmed.
doha on festival bath rush and no real change
festival bath, no change
One plunge at the holy hour, and the ledger of sins is said to be closed; but who will close the book of the mind?
After the festival dip, my cousin boasted that he had washed away all his faults and promptly picked up his old quarrel with his brother. A doha for him?
The singer on the bank of the holy waters plays his one-string lute after bathing, and sings about purity, but he bullies the little boy who carries his bag. Doha about him?
A doha about the singer who bathes in the holy waters at dawn, plays a one-string lute and sings of purity to the crowd, though his mind is full of vanity and not even a note of humility.
One-string lute in tune, body bathed, mind out of tune with its Maker.
one-string lute, holy bath
doha: one-string lute and a holy dip, still not clean inside
My grandfather bathed daily in a holy tank for sixty years, and when I asked him whether it had helped, he smiled and said, 'It cleaned the dirt, not the debts.' Doha on this?
doha: bathing for sixty years and still thinking dirty thoughts
lifelong bathing, no purity
Sixty years of bathing, and not a day without a grudge.

Compose a doha on the man who has bathed daily in the sacred waters for sixty years and still holds old grudges, still envies his neighbours, still cheats the poor, and still believes himself to be a pure man.
A verse about the furnace of the mind, which burns with desire and anger even after the pot of water has been poured, and the holy bath is no more effective than pouring a pot of water on it.
furnace, pot of water, bath
Pour a pot of water on the furnace, and it only hisses; bathe in holy waters, the mind only burns.
In our village the potter's furnace roars all day, and the old men say the bath in the holy pond is like pouring a pot of water on it, it cools the skin and nothing else. Doha?
doha: pouring a pot of water on a furnace, like bathing to wash the mind
The mountain meets the mosque in the sacred waters, but the man that dips remains small.
We drove to a holy ghat at the foot of a mountain, next to a mosque, and people from both faiths were bathing and arguing over parking. It made me think. Doha?
mountain, mosque, ablution

A doha about the believers at the foot of the mountain, one group bathing in the sacred waters and the other washing before the mosque, each thinking their washing purifies, while only the mind needs it.
doha: bathing near the mountain and the mosque, rituals of washing but same dirty minds
He bathes the body in holy waters, but who bathes the mind in the waters of love?
I asked my friend why he goes to bathe at every major festival, and he said, 'To wash away sins.' But he was the one who owes me money for three years. Can you write a doha?
write a doha about dirty minds and clean bodies
A Kabir style doha: if bathing in the holy waters could end sin, it would be a bargain for every sinner, and the pious would avoid the bath most, for they most believe in it.
clean body, dirty mind
salt, potter and clay, bathing

A doha about how salt dissolves in water and the potter shapes clay with water, but no amount of water will dissolve the salt of pride or soften the hard clay of the heart that does not wish to change.
Salt melts in the sacred waters and clay softens in the potter's hands, but the salt of pride does not.
doha: potter and clay and salt, water can't fix the mind
In our colony the potter says that clay gets softer with water, and salt melts too, but my neighbour who bathes every morning remains hard and bitter. Doha for him?
The shadow bathes along with the body and emerges as dark as before.
A verse about the pilgrim who bathes and tells himself he has left his sins behind in the sacred waters, though his shadow, which is his own conduct, stays attached and follows him up the bank.
shadow, holy dip
doha: your shadow comes out of the water with you
I saw my own shadow on the wet steps at the ghat after the dip and thought, if the sins were gone the shadow might lighten too. Can you make a doha from that?
A bottle of holy water for a hot temper; the cure is quiet within.
My aunt visits the holy waters every full night of the month to wash away family sins and brings back a bottle of water for us all. She thinks it will cure my bad temper. Doha?

Write a doha about the people who carry home a jar of sacred water from the pilgrimage and sprinkle it over the family, believing it cleans them of all faults, while no one cleans the habits that make faults.
doha on bringing home holy water as a cure for sins
holy water, no cure
thief, holy dip
doha: a thief takes a holy dip and goes back to stealing
The thief bathes in sacred waters, then returns to the dark street with clean hands.
A doha about the thief who goes to the sacred waters, bathes, prays for forgiveness, and goes straight to his next robbery, thinking the bath has made him fresh and his sins forgotten.
The thief who robbed our family store last year went on a pilgrimage and bathed in the holy waters, and was back to his old tricks within a month. A doha?
doha: bathing at the well every morning and lying all day
My grandmother said the old well in our village has holy water because pilgrims used to bathe there, but the neighbour who bathes in it daily cheats at cards. A doha?
Write a doha on the man who draws water from the well every morning, bathes with great ceremony, and then tells lies all day to everyone he meets, treating the bath as a shield for his character.
Bathing at the well each dawn, he draws up nothing but the water.
well, bathing, hollow
The lion tamer in our circus bathed in the holy waters before each show and said it protected him, but the lion bit him anyway. A doha for that irony?
A doha about the lion which fears no sin and is never bathed in the sacred waters, yet lives truthfully by its nature, while the pilgrim who bathes daily lives in falsehood by his choices.
The lion needs no holy bath, and its nature is clean; the pilgrim bathes and his nature is not.
doha: lion doesn't need a bath to be pure, humans do and still fail
lion, holy bath

A doha on the elephant, which bathes in the water and throws dust on its back the moment it comes out, like the pilgrim and the priest who bathe in the holy waters and then plunge again into their sins.
elephant, priest, holy bath
The elephant bathes and throws dust on its back; the priest bathes and throws sin on his soul.
At the ghat, an elephant bathed and then threw dust on itself, and the priest next to me who had just finished his own bath laughed, then immediately cursed a rickshaw driver. Doha on this?
doha: elephant bathes and throws dust right after, like a priest after a holy dip
doha: counting prayer beads in the holy dip, mind not in it
Prayer beads dripping with holy water, a mind dry as dust.
prayer beads, bath

A doha about the pilgrim who stands in the holy waters turning prayer beads, mumbling chants, believing both the water and the beads have cleansed him, though his mind is somewhere far, busy with trade and gossip.
I saw a woman in the holy waters rolling her prayer beads with a faraway look, and then complaining loudly at the person next to her. A doha for her?

Write about the tongue that chants holy names after the sacred bath and also spreads cruel gossip before the day is over, as the pilgrim crosses the bridge to the holy bank to wash and returns the same.
doha: tongue says holy names after a holy dip then gossips, bridge to the bank
tongue, bridge, bathing
The tongue bathed and sings; the bridge to the heart remains uncrossed.
After his holy dip, my uncle's tongue was as sharp as ever and he crossed the bridge to the stalls and started bargaining for the cruelest price. A doha for him?

A verse about the pilgrim who journeys a thousand miles to bathe in the sacred waters and complains of the cost, the cold, the crowds and his companions, as though purity could be bought without patience.
costly pilgrimage, complaints
doha: he travelled for the holy bath but complained the whole way
He crossed half the land to be purified, and brought his grumbling along.
My uncle took a long train journey for the holy dip and grumbled about the food and bunks from start to finish. A doha, please?
The sand on the bank holds the pilgrims' footprints and a one-string lute's last note; the same sand holds the same sins.
doha: sand on the bank, a one-string lute playing, pilgrims washing, still sinners

A doha about the pilgrims who gather on the sand at the water's edge, listening to a one-string lute and bathing at dawn, who go home with grains of sand in their sandals and the same sin in their hearts.
On the sand by the holy waters a man sat playing a one-string lute while the pilgrims bathed, and one of them stole his bowl while he played. Can you do a doha on this?
sand, one-string lute, bathing
Wash the body, wash the body, and the mind laughs behind its mask.
doha on how rituals for cleansing dont work if your mind is dirty
My brother dips into the holy waters every year and never apologizes to our sister for the way he treated her. Is there a doha for him?
Compose a doha on the one who believes that his annual bath in the sacred waters will cancel all his debts to people and to God, though there is not a trace of repentance in his heart.
annual bath, no repentance
My friend's grandfather says he bathed in all seven holy places in his life, and still he cannot sit for a minute in peace. A doha about his journey?
seven holy baths
A doha about the old man who has bathed in all the holy places in the land, collected all the sacred water in bottles, and yet finds no peace within, because he sought it in water and not in himself.
He has bathed in every holy water, and thirsts still.
doha: bathed everywhere, still restless
In the temple waters pilgrims wash and anoint with sandalwood, but the Lord waits in the clean heart alone.
Our temple has a sacred tank where everyone bathes before darshan, then smears sandalwood on their foreheads and leaves a trail of litter. Doha for our temple?
temple, bath, sandalwood
doha: bathing at the temple tank and putting on sandalwood but being rude
Compose a doha about the devotees who bathe at the temple tank, apply sandalwood paste to their skin, and walk in to pray, though their conduct outside the temple is rude, selfish and deceitful.
doha: the cleric says wash before prayer but not the mind
Wash the hands, wash the feet, wash the face; says the cleric, and the mind sits unwashed in the front row.
The cleric near us makes everyone wash carefully before prayer but gossips about members of the congregation. A doha, please?
A doha on the cleric who insists on the correct washing before prayer, hands, mouth, and feet, but never asks how the washing can matter if the thoughts are unwashed and the speech is unkind.
cleric, washing, hollow
bier, mosque, washing
Whether the body is washed for the mosque or for the bier, the one who washes it is what matters.

A doha on how we wash before the mosque, and wash the body before the bier, all for the sake of outer cleanliness, while the one thing that needs washing, the heart, is left unwashed until the very last moment.
doha: washing before the mosque and washing the body for the bier, same thing
When my uncle died, the elders washed his body for the bier with great care and the same men washed at the mosque before prayer, and no one asked about the heart. Doha?

A doha about the yogi who bathes daily in the holy waters and fasts to keep his body pure, but who feels anger rise the moment anyone interrupts his meditation, proving that water has not touched the mind.
yogi, holy bath
A yogi at our village pond bathes every dawn and sits with eyes shut, but throws a fit if a child splashes near him. Could you write a doha?
The yogi bathed his body, and his temper bathed in the same water.
doha: yogi takes holy baths and gets angry anyway
bath, bad habits
doha: wash away sins by bathing seems too easy
My roommate takes a long bath every Sunday and says it washes away his week's mistakes. By Monday he's in the same bad habits again. Doha for this?
Sunday's bath, Monday's sin; the cycle goes on like a wheel of wash and mud.

Write a doha on the person who bathes at the start of every week believing the water washes his faults, and finds that every week the same faults return, because water does not change what the mind chooses.
At the crossroads of the pilgrim path the beggar sits unwashed; the pilgrim passes by with his clean skin and a closed hand.

A doha about the pilgrim who bathes in the holy waters and walks to the crossroads, where a beggar sits shivering and hungry, and passes him by as if the beggar did not exist, his purity being only skin deep.
doha: pilgrim after his holy dip ignores a beggar at the crossroads
crossroads, beggar, holy bath
After bathing in the holy waters, our family walked past a beggar at the crossroads without a glance, and the thought stayed with me. Could you write a doha?
The mirror shows a clean face after the bath, and the snake of anger sleeps coiled behind it.
After my holy bath, I looked into the mirror and saw a clean face, and then a snake of a thought crossed my mind about a rival. Could you write a doha for this?
A doha on how the mirror reflects the washed face of the pilgrim who has bathed in the sacred waters, but cannot show the snake of poison coiled in his mind, which has remained unwashed.
mirror, snake, bathing
doha: mirror shows clean face, snake in the heart after a holy dip
doha: stuck in a cage of bad habits wrapped in a shroud of ego even after holy baths
A doha about the bird in a cage who bathes daily in the water bowl its keeper provides, and the pilgrim wrapped in a shroud of habit who bathes daily in the holy waters, neither of them any freer.
The bird bathes in its cage; the pilgrim bathes in a shroud of habit.
cage, shroud, holy dip
My grandmother, who has hardly left her room for years like a bird in a cage, takes the longest baths and asks if a shroud would be cleaner. Doha for that?
palace, paras, bath
doha: palace bath, the paras alchemist's touch, none of it cleans the mind
Neither the marble palace baths nor the legendary paras, the alchemist's touch, can wash the mind.
The king of our local story bathed daily in his palace with scented oils and sought the paras, the alchemist's touch, to cleanse himself, but never his heart. Doha idea?

A doha on the ruler in his palace who searches for the paras, the alchemist's touch, and bathes in fragrant waters daily to be pure, though neither the search nor the bath can scrub the arrogance from his mind.
peacock, holy bath
A doha about the peacock which dances in the rain without any ritual and is more beautiful than the pilgrim who dips in the sacred waters each year, with all his rites and none of the natural joy.
The peacock in our garden dances in the rain, no bath needed, while my uncle goes to bathe in the holy waters every year and remains grumpy. Doha on that?
The peacock dances in the rain, free of the holy dip, and the bathed pilgrim does not dance.
doha: peacock in the rain is purer than the pilgrim who bathes
A doha about the one who prides himself on how many times he has bathed in the sacred waters, counts the dips like a miser counts coins, and thinks the count is the measure of his purity.
counting holy dips
Count the dips, count the sins; the number of one does not cancel the other.
doha: counting your holy dips like points
My uncle keeps a diary of every holy dip he has taken, thirty one so far, and he is rude to every waiter he meets. Doha?
A doha about the leaf which floats on the water and is never wet, like the mind of one who truly knows, while the pilgrim who bathes in the sacred waters is soaked and the mind stays dry.
doha: the leaf floats on water but never gets wet, a metaphor for holy dips
I watched a leaf float on the water at the ghat while pilgrims bathed, and the leaf looked cleaner than any of them. Can you write a doha?
leaf, holy water
The leaf floats on the water untouched; the pilgrim bathes in it and is not cleansed.
The traveler washes his feet at the holy ghat and carries a jar of milk to offer, but not a drop to the hungry on the way.
A doha on the traveler who stops at the holy waters, bathes with a clean conscience, offers milk to the sacred bank, and passes by the hungry child on the road without a word or a coin.
traveler, milk, holy dip
On our trip to the holy dip, a traveler carried milk in a pot to offer at the water, while his own child was begging for a glass. A doha for that scene?
doha: traveler pouring milk into the holy water instead of giving it to hungry people
